title: The Sound Behind a Broken Bowl
paras: At a small museum of rural life, researcher Leila Sen tested whether background sounds changed people's emotional responses to damaged objects. Twenty-four adult volunteers examined the same [[fragment|fragment]] of a painted bowl. First, in silence, they wrote a short account of how it might have broken and rated their feelings towards it.

A week later, they returned and were randomly assigned to three groups. One heard a [[bamboo|bamboo]] flute, another listened to [[rap|rap]], and the third worked in silence again. Both recordings were original compositions, and their creators retained [[copyright|copyright]] while permitting their use in the experiment. Each participant had ten minutes to [[accomplish|accomplish]] the same writing task, with sound played at a comfortable volume.

The most [[striking|striking]] change concerned the stories rather than the emotion ratings. With music, more volunteers imagined relationships between people. Tomas, a retired [[shepherd|shepherd]], described an owner complaining [[bitterly|bitterly]] after a family argument ended with the bowl being dropped. Previously, he had simply described an accident. Another volunteer's initial [[disgust|disgust]] at the bowl's dirty surface became curiosity about who had used it.

However, average emotion ratings differed little between groups, and the sample was too small to establish whether either musical style had a distinct effect. The museum nevertheless decided to [[abolish|abolish]] its long-standing silence-only rule for storytelling sessions, while keeping quiet sessions available. Music had not reliably made the object more pleasant; it had offered some visitors another route into its possible human history.
zh: 在一家小型乡村生活博物馆，研究员莱拉·森测试了背景声音是否会改变人们对破损物品的情绪反应。二十四名成年志愿者观察了同一块彩绘碗的碎片。首先，他们在安静的环境中简短描述了这只碗可能如何破碎，并对自己面对它时的感受进行了评分。
一周后，他们再次来到博物馆，被随机分成三组。一组听竹笛音乐，一组听说唱音乐，第三组则仍在安静的环境中完成任务。两段录音均为原创作品，创作者保留版权，同时允许实验使用。每位参与者都有十分钟完成同样的写作任务，声音的播放音量让人感觉舒适。
最显著的变化体现在故事中，而非情绪评分上。伴随着音乐，更多志愿者想象出了人与人之间的关系。退休牧羊人托马斯描写道，一场家庭争吵以碗掉落告终，随后碗的主人愤愤地抱怨。此前，他只是描述了一次意外。另一位志愿者最初对碗上脏污表面的厌恶，则变成了对其使用者的好奇。
不过，各组的平均情绪评分差别很小，而且样本量不足以确定两种音乐风格是否各自具有独特效果。尽管如此，博物馆还是决定取消故事创作活动长期以来必须保持安静的规定，同时继续提供安静场次。音乐并未稳定地使这件物品变得更讨人喜欢，却为一些参观者提供了另一条路径，去探索它背后可能存在的人间往事。

q.s: The musicians were paid equal amounts for allowing their recordings to be used.
q.why: 只提到授权使用，未说明报酬。

q.s: Tomas's first account described the bowl being broken deliberately.
q.why: 他最初描述的是一次意外。

q.s: The museum continued to offer quiet storytelling sessions after changing its rule.
q.why: 末段明确说明更改规定后仍保留安静场次。
